{{Short description|Mathematical constant}}
[[File:Foias constant sequence.png|thumb|400px|Evolution of the sequence <math>x_{n+1} = (1 + 1/x_n)^n</math> for several values of <math>x_1</math>, around the Foias constant <math>\alpha</math>. Evolution for <math>x_1 = \alpha</math> is in green. Other initial values lead to two accumulation points, 1 and <math>\infty</math>. A [[logarithmic scale]] is used.]]
In [[mathematical analysis]], the '''Foias constant''' is a [[real number]] named after [[Ciprian Foias]].

It is defined in the following way: [[for every]] real number ''x''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;>&nbsp;0, there is a [[sequence]] defined by the [[recurrence relation]]
: <math> x_{n+1} = \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x_n} \right)^n</math>
for ''n'' = 1, 2, 3, ....  The Foias constant is the unique choice ''&alpha;'' such that if ''x''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''&alpha;'' then the sequence [[divergent sequence|diverges]] to infinity.  For all other values of ''x''<sub>1</sub>, the sequence is divergent as well, but it has two [[accumulation point|accumulation points]]: 1 and infinity.<ref name="Foias">Ewing, J. and Foias, C. "An Interesting Serendipitous Real Number." In ''Finite versus Infinite: Contributions to an Eternal Dilemma'' (Ed. C. Calude and G. Păun). London: Springer-Verlag, pp. 119–126, 2000.</ref>  Numerically, it is
: <math> \alpha = 1.187452351126501\ldots</math>.<ref name="OEIS">{{Cite OEIS|sequencenumber=A085848 |name=Decimal expansion of Foias's Constant}}</ref>
The constant can be computed by solving backwards:
<math> x_{n} = \frac{1}{\sqrt[n]{x_{n+1}} - 1}</math>

This recursion converges for any starting value <math> x_n\ne 0</math><ref name="OEIS"/>.

When ''x''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''&alpha;'' then the growth rate of the sequence (''x''<sub>''n''</sub>) is given by the [[Limit of a sequence|limit]]
: <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} x_n \frac{\log n}n = 1, </math>
where "log" denotes the [[natural logarithm]].<ref name="Foias" />

The same methods used in the proof of the uniqueness of the Foias constant may also be applied to other similar recursive sequences.<ref>{{citation|last = Anghel|first = Nicolae| title = Foias numbers|journal = An. Ştiinţ. Univ. "Ovidius" Constanţa Ser. Mat.|volume = 26| year = 2018| issue = 3| pages = 21–28 | doi = 10.2478/auom-2018-0030|s2cid = 195842026| url = https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1705461/m2/1/high_res_d/18440835-Analele_Universitatii_Ovidius.pdf}}</ref>
